newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SOCCER-AUSTRALIAN CLUBS FACE EXPULSION AFTER CROWD TROUBLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUSTRALIAN CLUBS FACE EXPULSION AFTER CROWD TROUBLE.

text.p: Two of Australia's leading soccer clubs face expulsion from the national league next season after crowd violence involving rival ethnic Greek and Croat fans at a cup semifinal on Sunday.

Ruling body Soccer Australi` said on Monday Sydney United and South Melbourne would be thrown out of the league if they were found guilty of bringing the game into disrepute by failing to control their fans.

Fighting broke out when police tried to stop the Sydney team's fans -- traditionally of Croatian origin -- celebrating the only goal of the match by lighting illegal flares. Two officers sent into the stands were attacked by fans.
After the match more than 1,000 United fans invaded the pitch and clashed with Melbourne supporters, some of whom were carrying a Serbian flag to taunt ther rivals.
Three people were arrested and five police officers suffered minor injuries.
Soccer Australia has been involved in a dispute with top clubs over the sport's ethnic profile and last year forced three clubs to scrap logos reflecting their European ethnic roots.
Sydney United dra their support almost exclusively from Sydney's Croat community, while South Melbourne are backed by the city's large Greek population.

"We had demonstrations in support of Croatian nationalism and demonstrations in support of Greek nationalism and there is no place for that in soccer, nor in Australian society," Soccer Australia chairman David Hill told a news conference.
"We are establishing our own inquiry and we will be charging both clubs with bringing the game into disrepute," Hill said.
"We are absolutely resolute it (crowd violence) will not happen again and any club that delivers that to soccer will be out."
Hill said the inquiry would take about one month to complete.
